newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut jails journalists for slandering Saudi king.
newsitem.headline: Beirut jails journalists for slandering Saudi king.

text.p: A Beirut judge sentenced on Thursday the owner and the director of a pro-Libyan weekly magazine to 60 days in jail each for slandering Saudi Arabia's King Fahd, judicial sources said.

The verdict stated that Walid al-Husseini, owner of Al-Kifah al-Arabi, and its responsible director Taleb Abdallah were guilty of insulting the king "in a 1995 article titled: What if we get a Sri Lankan custodian for Jerusalem".
Husseini and Abdallah were each fined the sum of 50 million Lebanese pounds ($322,000).
The sources said the journalists who did not attend the verdict session would remain free pending an appeal to a higher court.
The verdict quoted parts of the article which appeared in the October 30 issue of last year.

"Mentioned in the article was that Jerusalem is a holy shrine and King Fahd who declared himself custodian of the holy shrines...purchased 61 commerical planes from the United States one day after the decision of the U.S. Congress," the verdict said.
On October 24 last year, the Congress approved a bill to move the U.S. embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem by May 1999 -- a decision that angered the Arab world.

"If we get a custodian from Sri Lanka or the Phillipines like those found in most Saudi homes, wouldn't he be more protective when it comes to Jerusalem or has the holy shrine become a dull old memory," the verdict quoted the article as saying.

In October 1986, King Fahd changed his title from Majesty to "The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques" -- Islam's holiest shrines at the Saudi cities of Mecca and Medina. Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque is the third holiest shrine to Moslems.
The court case was brought against the pro-Libyan magazine by the country's prosecutor general under article 23 of Lebanon's publication law.

The article -- which gives the prosecution the right to file the lawsuit -- states that slandering, insulting or humiliating foreign presidents, kings or heads of states in the press is punishable by up to two years imprisonment and up to 100 million Lebanese pounds fine.
